abstract: In this paper, we propose a new approach to construct quasi-cyclic low-density parity-check (QC-LDPC) codes using Hamming codewords of weight three, namely the HM-QC-LDPC codes. Thanks to the distance property of Hamming codes, length four cycles are avoided from the Tanner graph of the constructed codes, resulting in codes of girth six. This approach can be further extended to construct QC-LDPC codes of girth eight. Our numerical results show that the proposal has a better cycle profile than the progressive-edge-growth (PEG) constructed codes, and consequently prevails in performance. Moreover, the constructed QC-LDPC code prevails the LDPC code of the IEEE802.22 standard by 0.2 dB at the bit error rate (BER) of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> when the codeword length is within hundreds of bits, making it a promising candidate for scenarios where strict decoding latency is imposed.

articleTitle: Modified two-dimensional compressed sensing scheme for massive MIMO channel estimation
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The problem of compressed sensing (CS) is considered in two-dimensional (2D) sparse decomposition measurement model. Correspondingly, a novel recovery algorithm - modified 2D subspace pursuit (M-2DSP) algorithm is proposed with the available prior support and chunk sparse structure. The massive multi-input multi-out (MIMO) system show a concealed sparse structure and temporal correlation in the user (UE) channel matrix in virtue of the shared local scatterers in the physical propagation environment. Thereby the proposed scheme can be applied to sparse channel estimation in massive MIMO systems with temporal correlation. Furthermore its effectiveness is proved, both theoretical analysis and experiment simulations testify the usefulness and advantages of the new algorithm in recovery performance, especially in smaller overhead training pilot quantity and lower transmit signal noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: An energy-efficient design for multihop relay network adopting CC-HARQ scheme
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper investigates the energy-efficient design of a multihop relay network adopting the Chase Combining based Hybrid Automatic Repeat reQuest (CC-HARQ) scheme with sum power constraint from a cross-layer perspective. We aim at maximizing the energy efficiency (EE) in the multihop relay network by jointly optimizing the payload length and average transmission energy per bit over all hops, with no limitation on the total number of (re)transmissions times. The theoretical findings are verified by simulations and the impacts of various parameters, e.g., the modulation and coding scheme (MCS) levels, channel gains and transmission distance, on EE are studied in detail. The results demonstrate that significant energy saving can be achieved by the proposed joint optimum algorithm.

articleTitle: Dense optical flow computation using textural features
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper proposes a new algorithm for dense optical flow computation. It combines Gabor filter texture description in a variational framework. The textural features with spatial Gabor filter group are used as an extension to the original bright constant model. The corresponding global energy functional is established, and the flow field at each pixel of the image is iteratively computed by solving the corresponding discretized Euler-Lagrange equations. Performances of the algorithm are tested on real and synthetic sequences, and are compared with other dense optical flow computation techniques, which demonstrate a great improvement on the convergence rate and robustness against brightness changes.

articleTitle: A data collection approach based on mobile sinks for heterogeneous sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In wireless sensor networks, the limitation of energy and cache space of nodes around the base station, as well as the multi-hop transmission instability will seriously interfere the performance of traditional data collection protocols. To address this problem, a data collection mechanism by using mobile base station is proposed. Firstly, a new clustering algorithm-Time High-Overflow-Based Dominating (THD) is proposed that the sensor network is divided into several clusters based on sample rate and cache of nodes. Secondly, temporary caching mechanism (TCM) is proposed to further resolve the buffer overflow problem. Finally, Dominating-Based Minimum Weighted Sum (DMWS) protocol is proposed in order to design the optimal path of the mobile base stations. The simulation results show that: compared with traditional data collection schemes, the method shortens the moving distance of the mobile base station, extends the network life cycle reduces the energy consumption, and has the shorter delay of the data.

articleTitle: Resource and power allocation for Uplink LTE networks with load and power coupling
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we aim to minimize the total transmission power in uplink LTE networks where mutual interference exists among cells. We use the signal-to-interference-noise-ratio (SINR) coupling model to characterize the mutual relation. By analyzing the SINR coupling model, we prove that operating at minimal rate and maximal load is optimal in minimizing the total transmission power. To solve the power minimization problem, we develop a distributed resource and power allocation algorithm. This algorithm is proved to be convergent. Numerical results show that our proposed algorithm achieves better performance compared to the conventional scheme in terms of total power consumption.

articleTitle: Wavelet frame truncated ℓ1-regularized image deblurring
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In the past decades, wavelet frame models for image restoration have been extensively studied, main reason is due to its good capability of sparsely estimating the piecewise smooth functions like natural images. The ℓ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> norm of wavelet frame coefficients are penalized as the regularization term is widespread in these models. In this work, we propose a truncated ℓ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-regularized model, besides the classical sparsity prior, we exploit the support information of wavelet frame coefficients to further improve the recovery performance. We use efficient alternating direction method to solve this resulted model. Compared with the current state-of-the-art deblurring methods, numerical experiments validate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: A novel anomaly detection with temporal and spatial aggregation in mobile networks
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Mobile networks are becoming more and more advanced, and various internet terminals are accessible. These all call for an increased reliability and stability on cellular networks, especially internet service in cellular networks. In this paper, we propose a new anomaly detection method for periodic network parameters. We use aggregation, including threshold aggregation (TA) and spatial aggregation, to enhance the periodicity of parameters. TA can smooth the small fluctuation when a parameter is in valley and improve the accuracy of anomaly detection. Spatial aggregation uses an unsupervised way which is widely applied in Big Data Analysis to cluster similar base stations (BSs). In each cluster, the periodicity of parameters is highlighted. Our experiments, which are based on real data from current cellular networks, show that, compared with the detection in equal time bins (e.g., hourly aggregation) and settled space (e.g., BS), our aggregation method improves the detection results efficiently.

articleTitle: A channel coding approach for physical-layer authentication
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: For physical-layer authentication, the authentication tags are often sent concurrently with messages without much bandwidth expansion. In this paper, we present a channel coding approach for physical-layer authentication. The generation of authentication tags can be formulated as an encoding process for an ensemble of codes, where the shared key between Alice and Bob is considered as the input and the message is used to specify a code from the ensemble of codes. Then, we show that the security of physical-layer authentication schemes can be analyzed through decoding and physical-layer authentication schemes can achieve some degree of information-theoretic security.

articleTitle: An effective method for automatic recognition of Turbo codes
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Due to the more complexity of Turbo code than linear block code and convolutional code, the existing methods for identifying channel coding cannot be directly applied to Turbo codes. This paper proposes a method for automatic recognition of Turbo codes. The proposed method firstly demultiplexes and de-punctures the soft information of the received sequence to attain the soft information of two sequences corresponding to the output of component encoders. Then the soft information of punctured bits is patched. Finally, the method for automatic recognition of convolution codes is used to recognize the component encoders, puncture structure and interleaver. Consequently, the Turbo codes used in transmitters is recognized. Simulation results show that the proposed method can quickly and effectively complete the automatic recognition of Turbo codes and is easy to implement.

articleTitle: Dynamical modelling collective behavior through adaptation to topological neighbors
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In recent years the field studies on collective behaviors have revealed that topological interaction of k nearest neighbors plays a the key role in flocking. In this work, we show a model of flocking through adaptation to k nearest topological neighbors, and examine the influence of the number of topological neighbors on flocking dynamics with different group size. The model is validated by simulations.

articleTitle: Prediction-based pricing for request outsourcing in cloud federation
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Cloud federation is a recently proposed paradigm that advocates resource sharing among multiple cloud providers (CPs). In cloud federation, the demanding CPs with resource limitation can outsource their requests to other supplying CPs with idle resources. Pricing places an important role in incentivizing the resource sharing among the CPs. In this paper, we consider the cloud federation with one supplying CPs and multiple demanding CPs. We propose a prediction-based pricing scheme to maximize the social welfare for the case with incomplete information. We also analyze the impact of prediction error and derive the worst-case lower bound of the efficiency of our proposed prediction-based pricing scheme.

articleTitle: A nonlinear and non-Gaussian distributed fusion based on Rao-Blackwellized particle filtering
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In nonlinear and non-Gaussian multi-sensor fusion scenarios, the Covariance Intersection (CI) algorithm is utilized to fuse estimations from distributed sensors, in which targets are commonly tracked by a family of Particle Filtering (PF) algorithm. Furthermore, standard PF can be replaced by Rao-Blackwellized PF (RBPF) based on linear/nonlinear State Space models to produce more accurate means and variances for CI fusion. Unfortunately, the RBPF algorithm fails in conventional radar systems because their observations contain no information about the linear part of target state. To overcome such an issue, a Kalman Estimation based BRPF (KE-BRPF) algorithm is proposed to form a novel distributed CI fusion. In KE-RBPF, the correlation between linear and nonlinear parts of target state is investigated. Benefitting from this investigation, the linear part of target state is correctly tracked based on the nonlinear one. Finally, the simulations verify that our KE-RBPF-CI fusion outperforms other PF-based CI fusions, in terms of means and deviations.

articleTitle: An atmospheric noise suppression method based on synchrosqueezed wavelet transform
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Low frequency radio wave has efficient long-range propagation in the so-called earth-ionosphere waveguide and it is widely used in communication and navigation. However, low frequency radio wave is suffered from intensive atmospheric noise. In order to extract signal of interest from atmospheric noise, adaptive soft limiter is used to suppress the impulsiveness of the atmospheric noise. And then the newly emerged synchrosqueezed wavelet transform (SST) method is adopted for the time-frequency filtering for the atmospheric noise. Simulation results show that, the proposed method outperforms the wavelet denoising method from qualitative and quantitative analysis.

articleTitle: An energy-aware chunk selection mechanism in HTTP video streaming
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In recent years, video streaming has contribute 40% traffic in LTE wireless networks. However, battery has been a bottleneck for user to enjoy the high quality video since the progress of battery technique is far less than the advancement of wireless technique. How to enable users to enjoy video streaming given limited battery is an urgent problem. In this paper, we propose a video transmission mechanism which optimize the chunk size of HTTP streaming by taking into account the user watching behavior and characteristics of LTE networks. Numerical results shows our mechanism can save energy apparently compared with existing schemes.

articleTitle: Anchor graph hashing with semantically consistent graph
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Hashing has become a popular technique for fast similarity search in massive databases. However, learning compact binary codes which accelerates similarity search remains a challenge. In order to reduce the computational complexity of mapping semantically similar data to close codes, an anchor graph hashing (AGH) approach is used to build an approximate neighborhood graph using anchor graph, which allows constant time hashing of a new data point by extrapolating graph Laplacian eigenvectors to eigenfunctions. However, the Euclidean distance is mostly used to construct the anchor graph Laplacian in AGH, which may not reflect the semantic similarity of the data points. In this paper, we propose a method to directly optimize the anchor graph Laplacian directly based on the label smoothness and the rank pairwise loss function in the hash function learning process. The learned anchor graph, which represents the semantic similarity better between data points and anchors, is then applied to AGH for effective binary code learning. Extensive simulations are conducted on the publicly available dataset to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A multiphase level set clustering approach using MRF-based Student's-t mixture model
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Student's-t distribution has attracted widely attention on model-based clustering analysis. In this paper, we propose a new level set energy function framework where the Markov random field-based Student's-t mixture model is incorporated for clustering both static images and time-series data. This algorithm provides a general strategy by taking the best of Bayesian technique and level set formulation. A remarkable advantage of the proposed method is that it can overcome the weakness of the classical level set method by filtering out the outliers and stopping at the boundary points. It is mainly because the proposed technique models the probability density function of the data via Student's-t mixture model. Another attractive feature is that the local relationship among neighboring pixels is considered into mixture model so that the proposed framework is more robust against noise compared to the other level set based models. Expectation maximization algorithm is applied to obtain model parameters by maximizing the log-likelihood function. Additionally, the proposed model has simplified structure which sharply reduces the computational complexity. Finally, numerical experiments on various synthetic, real-world images, and time-series data are conducted. The performances are compared to other related approaches in terms of effectiveness and accuracy.

articleTitle: Who care for channel sparsity? Robust sparse recursive least square based channel estimation
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In the next-generation wireless communication systems, the broadband signal transmission over wireless channel often incurs the frequency-selective channel fading behavior and also results in the channel sparse structure which is dominant by very few large coefficients. To ensure the stable wireless propagation, various linear adaptive channel estimation algorithms, e.g., recursive least square (RLS) and least mean square (LMS), have been developed. However, the traditional algorithms are unable to exploit the channel sparsity. Supporting by the compressive sensing (CS) theory, channel estimation performance can be further improved by taking advantage of the sparsity. In this paper, RLS based fast adaptive sparse channel estimation algorithm is proposed by introducing two sparse constraint functions, L1-norm and L0-norm. To improve the flexibility of the proposed algorithms, this paper introduces a regularization parameter selection method to adaptively exploit the channel sparsity. Finally, Monte Carlo based computer simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms based robust channel estimation either for sparse or non-sparse channel.

articleTitle: TDD reciprocity compensation for massive MIMO system with iterative calibration
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Channel reciprocity is a key characteristic in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems in time division duplex (TDD) mode, by which the downlink channel state information (CSI) can be obtained easily. However, the hardware mismatch of the transceiver radio frequency (RF) chains disables the channel reciprocity. Considering the application complexity of full calibration of massive MIMO, this paper focuses on partial calibration and obtains the upper bound of the system capacity based on the massive MIMO approximation theory. Then a novel iterative calibration (IC) method is proposed, which significantly reduces the complexity of partial channel calibration. Compared with the existing algorithms, simulations indicate that the proposed has only a slight decline in performance.

articleTitle: Achievable rate analysis for multi-pair AF massive MIMO systems with imperfect CSI
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-pair amplify-and-forward (AF) massive MIMO system is investigated, where multiple source users communicate with multiple destination users via a single relay. The achievable rate of the system and its analytical expression are studied for power-scaling laws when ZFT/ZFR algorithm is adopted at the relay. The imperfect channel state information (CSI) is considered and the MMSE estimator is utilized. Analytical consequences reveal that with the number of antennas growing into infinity, the effect of small-scale fading, the inter-user interference and the noise could be eliminated. And the achievable rate will be affected by channel errors, the number of users, and the power-scaling law. Simulation results effectively verify our analytical expressions.

Author Keywords: AF massive MIMO system ZFT/ZFR algorithm

articleTitle: Face recognition based on weighted wavelet transform and compressed sensing
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: A face recognition algorithm based on weighted wavelet transform and compressive sensing is proposed in this paper. Considering the influence of wavelet transform on each component, the low-frequency components, the horizontal and vertical components are weighted fused. It can reduce the loss of the identification information and the dimensionality of face images. Then, principal component analysis is employed to extract facial feature matrices. Each class of the test samples is reconstructed by the sparse coefficients and the dictionary matrix. The test samples are classified in the smallest residual error by comparing with the reconstructed samples. Experimental results on ORL and FERET face databases verify that the algorithm proposed in this paper has a better recognition ability. The recognition accuracy and recognition speed of the new algorithm are better than traditional methods.

articleTitle: A scrambling and encryption algorithm for selective block of identification photo
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: As identification photo being a significant part of personal information security, the encryption of identification photo has become a frontier subject. The encryption of identification photo, different from common image encryption, mainly focuses on the human facial region. Therefore, the key point is to distinguish the face details and background details accurately and to design an encryption algorithm with huge key space and sensitivity key. In this paper, we proposes an image algorithm for color identification photo by multi-layer block scrambling in frequency domain. After dividing the image into blocks and detecting the human facial region, we encrypt the facial region in frequency domain. In comparison with the commonly used image encryption algorithm, the experimental result shows that the proposed algorithm requires less amount of calculation, while simultaneously provides larger algorithm key space and more sensitive key.

articleTitle: Binary lossy coding problem with encoder side information and common reconstruction constraint
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The source coding problem with common reconstruction constraint is considered, where the encoder can produce an exact copy of the compressed source reconstructed by the decoder. In this paper, we consider the variation of this problem in which the encoder can observe the side information which may be different from the decoder side information. For the doubly-symmetric binary source, we derive the rate distortion function, and perform the utility of encoder side information.

articleTitle: A superposition scheme for downlink multicell processing with caching base stations
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: An achievability scheme is proposed for the multiple access diamond channel with two destinations, where each base station has cached a part of the messages intended for the destination nodes. This achievability scheme is the generalization of the scheme of sending correlated codewords with the superposition structure proposed for the 2-destination multiple access diamond channel. It is shown that the achievable rate region of the scheme we proposed is the same as the achievable region of the scheme of sending correlated codewords with the superposition structure proposed for the 2-destination multiple access diamond channel without caching, but with increased backhaul link capacities by the amount of the rate of the cached information. This shows the optimality of our scheme in terms of utilizing the cached message.

articleTitle: Impacts of outdated CSI for secure cooperative systems with opportunistic relay selection
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we study the secrecy outage probability (SOP) of an opportunistic relay selection scheme where an optimal relay is selected based on the delayed feedback from the multi-antenna destination. We present a new exact closed-form expression of the SOP, and two kinds of asymptotic form of SOP are further derived to explicitly show secrecy performance. In addition, we show that the SOP can be reduced by increasing the number of relays through analysis and simulation results. An important result show that the secrecy diversity order of the system has nothing to do with the number of relays with outdated CSI.

articleTitle: Object segmentation of indoor scenes using perceptual organization on RGB-D images
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we address the problem of object segmentation, which is important for further scene analysis and scene understanding. To improve the accuracy of object segmentation from the images with indoor scenes, we propose a new algorithm which combined perceptual organization method with color information and depth information. In the proposed algorithm, firstly, the gPb-ucm method is used for initial segmentation, and then, color information and depth information are both used for perceptual organization. Color information and depth information are combined to achieve a complementary effect, and on the basis of image foremost segmentation, the segmentation result is modified by perceptual organization. Experimental results demonstrate the proposed method can effectively improve the accuracy of object segmentation.

articleTitle: Joint user grouping and beamformer design for wireless backhaul in downlink cloud-RANs
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we consider beamformer design of access and backhaul links in downlink cloud-RANs. An optimization problem is formulated with the objective of maximizing the weighted sum rate (WSR) under the constraints of power consumption, backhaul rate, as well as user grouping, which assumes each user is served by only one SBS to reduce the traffic load over the backhaul links. To solve this intractable problem, reweighted ℓ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-norm, successive convex approximation and WMMSE-based formulation methods are introduced to transform it into a tractable form. An iterative algorithm based on block coordinate update (BCU) scheme is designed to solve the approximate problem. Finally, simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: An efficiently enhanced authenticated key exchange protocol for terminal to server environment
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: A typical Two-Party Authenticated Key Exchange Protocol aims to provide the information confidentiality between client and server in public network. The protocol has to satisfy some secure properties and possess the lower computational cost. The new protocol in this paper enhances the scheme of Chou, which has some flaws, such as the impersonation attack and public key problem. The enhanced scheme can resolve the problems by using the Elliptic Curve Cryptosystem to achieve an efficient program to distribute private key. Then the security analysis and performance evaluation were performed between our enhanced scheme and some other related works. The results show that the computational cost of our scheme is less than the others while satisfying the security requirement.

articleTitle: On the capacity of amplitude modulation based molecular communication channels
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This work focuses on the capacity analysis of molecular communication (MC) channel where the information is encoded in the number of the released molecules. By introducing molecule life expectancy equaling to a symbol interval, the channel is considered to be memoryless. The properties of the capacity-achieving input of this channel is deduced under the constraint of the peak released molecules at the transmitter. The capacity is computed numerically by using the cutting-plane algorithm. It is also proved that the channel capacity can be achieved through a bipolar input in a severe environment.

articleTitle: A multi-band power allocation scheme for green energy-efficient cognitive radio networks
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Green cognitive radio has attracted significant research attention as an effective means of alleviating spectrum scarcity and energy-saving problem in wireless communications. In this paper, we focus on the power allocation for maximizing the transmission throughput and energy efficiency (EE) of secondary users (SUs). More specifically, we propose a multi-band power allocation scheme, where multiple idle spectrum bands detected in spectrum sensing phase are simultaneously utilized for the secondary transmission. We formulate the power allocation between multiple detected idle spectrum bands with the consideration of mutual interference between the primary user (PU) and SU which is referred to as multi-band power allocation (MBPA). We prove that the formulated MBPA problem is convex and consider the use of sequential unconstrained minimization technique (SUMT) interior point method for solving the formulated problem. Finally, numerical results show the advantage of proposed MBPA scheme over conventional equal-power allocation (EPA) and best-band selection (BBS) methods in terms of the energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Speech reconstruction based on compressed sensing theory using smoothed L0 algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: At present, speech signals have good sparsity in frequency domain and discrete cosine transformation (DCT) domain etc. Therefore it can be researched based on compressed sensing (CS). CS compresses signals which are sparse or compressible at the sending end, and then reconstruct them at the receiving end. This paper proposes the compressed speech reconstruction method based smoothed L0 (SL0) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the SL0 algorithm can obtain a better performance than the traditional orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) method in reconstruction of speech signals.

articleTitle: Adaptive GoP dividing video coding for wireless broadcast based on power allocation optimization
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Based on analog joint source-channel coding (JSCC) scheme, SoftCast approach can gracefully avoid the cliff effect. And SoftCast is outperformed by the DCast scheme which combines JSCC scheme with distributed source coding (DSC) theory. Considering the disproportionate distribution of frequency coefficients, we propose an optimized power allocation SoftCast (OPA-SoftCast) scheme which has a significant performance improvement compared to SoftCast. In addition, we develop a novel adaptive GoP dividing video coding (AGD-Cast) scheme. It integrates the benefits of DCast and the proposed OPA-SoftCast. Compared to DCast scheme, AGD-Cast scheme effectively improves the quality of reconstructed I-frame, and it has better performance when scenarios of video source change rapidly.

articleTitle: Alleviating sensor location error using sources in unknown locations
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Alleviating sensor location error is essential for promoting the quality of various location based services. Compared with the existing approaches which utilize the calibrators with known locations, e.g., GPS, this paper investigates the calibration performance which uses only the measurements from sources in unknown locations. Since no reference information is involved, it is revealed in this paper that only part of sensor location uncertainty can be reduced. For example, in a network with six or more sensors, at least three sources are required for reducing the sensor relative location error by time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) measurements, while there still exists uncertainty in the network global location and orientation. The calibration performance under other measurements or sensor-source numbers is also provided, and the efficiency of the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) is confirmed in simulations.

articleTitle: Composite face sketch recognition based on components
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Composite face sketch recognition is a challenging problem in face recognition, which is important for law enforcement. Considering composite sketches are generated from facial components, a component-based representation approach was proposed to match composite sketches to photos recently. They extract features from each component and use the fusion of four most discriminative components as the final matching score. However, they ignore the inherent structure of composite sketch and the fusion does not take the full components' information into consideration. This paper presents a novel composite sketch recognition method by extracting two image feature descriptors from components, fusing them at score level, combining facial components with different weights. In addition, we show the detailed procedure of composite sketch generation, which is useful for building related composite database. Experiments on the public composite sketch database (E-PRIP) demonstrate that our proposed method achieves superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Link-level simulation of TDD-based massive MIMO system
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the link-level simulation of the time-division-duplex (TDD) based massive MIMO system employing OFDM technology. Influenced by the hardware mismatch between base station (BS) and mobile stations (MS), and the limitations of hardware implementation, the system model, simulation settings, and simulation procedures for uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) are presented to help develop a practical TDD-based massive MIMO system. The simulation settings and procedures list the details about the simulation platform, including the general parameters, LTE-like frame structure, resource grid of users (UEs), block diagrams of system, MIMO detection/precoding algorithm, and the reciprocity calibration method. We have evaluated the performance of system from the aspects of bit error rate (BER) and throughput. Numerical results show that the significance of the reciprocity calibration at the downlink for multi-user's data transmission, and the methods to improve system's throughput.

articleTitle: A self-normalized weighted bit-flipping decoding algorithm for LDPC codes
publicationTitle: 2016 8th International Conference on Wireless Communications & Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: A novel self-normalized weighted bit-flipping (SNWBF) decoding algorithm for low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes is proposed. Compared to the best known weighted bit-flipping decoding, the SNWBF algorithm converges significantly faster but with little performance penalty. For decoding of LDPC codes, the proposed SNWBF algorithm considers not only the reliability of the neighboring check nodes, but also the reliability of each variable node. Compared to the IMWBF algorithm, the proposed algorithm does not require multiplicative normalization and performs even better.
